reasoning_content:
Now let me verify the tiles actually render data (a tile request). It's Monaco only (bounds). Let me test a tile within Monaco bounds. And also test the frontend API connectivity. And confirm the whole stack works via the documented entry points.

Also verify the QGIS server is functional at a lower level — the qgis container health check passes GetCapabilities without MAP at root, so QGIS server itself works. The MAP-based request with .qgz fails because the placeholder project is invalid. But that's expected with no valid project. The README says a MAP parameter pointing to a valid project is required. Since none is provided, QGIS OWS can't fully serve, but that's a data prerequisite, not an installation defect.

Let me check the tile server serves actual tiles, and test the API from the frontend (SSR fetch uses internal backend URL). Let me check frontend page content for data or errors.

Let me also verify Caddy certs and that the frontend SSR finished loading (the page returned HTML). Check whether frontend logs show errors fetching API.

Let me test a tile.

echo "=== tile within Monaco z10 ==="; curl -sk --resolve tiles.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 -o /dev/null -w "10 z=%{http_code}\n" "https://tiles.localhost/data/germany/10/539/372.pbf"
echo "=== frontend page check for project data ==="; curl -skL --resolve app.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 https://app.localhost/ | grep -o "Default\|Fehler\|error\|Error" | sort | uniq -c | head
echo "=== frontend logs full ==="; docker logs qonnectra_frontend_dev 2>&1 | tail -30
